attack_assumption.attacker: Ordinary untrusted caller, request arguments, raw mappings, fixture rows, copied or syntactically valid ExactRef/receipt, and caller-controlled test helper outputs
attack_assumption.trusted: HQ-adopted exact warrant bootstrap, owner-controlled registrar journal, verifier independently provisioned from governance-approved trusted deployment root; no authority from user-provided payload
attack_assumption.not_defended: Arbitrary hostile Python code execution with write access to registrar/verifier process memory, monkeypatching privileged modules, malicious deployment maintainer or compromised HQ governance. Python-private state alone is not a cryptographic security boundary against hostile code.
attack_assumption.fork_if_required: If code-compromise/F7-style adversary is in scope, separate service/signed attestation and independently verified key custody need distinct HQ warrant; this bounded proposal does not claim it
attack_assumption.guarantee: Owner/data authority provenance against caller self-attestation, not general adversarial process-security
